case_name: K.Srinivas v. K. Sunita — full case name
facts_of_case: Marriage of parties celebrated in 1989, male child born in 1991, Respondent-Wife started suffering from Sheehan's syndrome. On 29th/30th June, 1995, Respondent left matrimonial house and filed criminal complaint against Appellant-Husband and family members. Appellant-Husband filed petition for divorce on ground of cruelty and irretrievable breakdown of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The filing of a false criminal complaint does not automatically prove matrimonial cruelty.
legal_principles.held: This power, however, has not been bestowed by our Constitution on any other Court. It is for these reasons that we have confined arguments only to the aspect of whether the filing of a false criminal complaint sufficiently proves matrimonial cruelty as would entitle the injured party to claim dissolution of marriage.

legal_principles.principle: The acquittal of the Appellant and his family members in a criminal complaint does not necessarily mean that the complaint was false.
legal_principles.held: What should be kept in perspective, it is reasonably argued, that the Complainant is not the controlling conductor in this Orchestra, but only one of the musicians who must deliver her rendition as and when and how she is called upon to do.

outcome.final_order: If a false criminal complaint is preferred by either spouse, it would invariably and indubitably constitute matrimonial cruelty, such as would entitle the other spouse to claim a divorce.

keywords: K. Srinivas Rao vs. D.A. Deepa
